def: To become less intense or widespread
example: The rain finally began to abate just as the school picnic was due to finish.

def: To carry someone off secretly and by force, especially against their will
example: Two masked men attempted to abduct the postman, who managed to call the emergency services.

def: Departing noticeably from what is normal or expected
example: The school counsellor called his behaviour aberrant, as no other pupil reacted so violently to a lost pen.

def: The comparative form of able, meaning more skilful than the rest
syn: most capable; most talented; most proficient
ant: least capable; most inept; most unskilled
example: Though only eleven, my cousin proved the ablest goalkeeper in the county tournament.

def: Extremely bad or unpleasant, causing disgust
example: The weather was abominable, so our sports day was cancelled and we sat in the dining hall instead.

def: Something so bad that it is regarded with disgust or horror
example: Everyone agreed that the amount of litter left in the park after the festival was an abomination.

def: Rough to the touch, and likely to rub the skin or hurt feelings
example: The kitchen sponge was abrasive enough to polish a dirty pan, but far too rough for washing my face.

def: The fact of a person or thing not being there when expected
example: Your absence from Tuesday's rehearsal will mean losing your place in the choir, so tell the director today.

def: Complete and without any doubt, limit or exception
example: There was absolute silence in the hall as the head teacher read out the examination results.

def: So completely interested in something that everything else is forgotten
example: She was absorbed in her new novel and did not hear the bell, or her mother calling her for tea.

def: Dealing with general ideas and qualities rather than particular things
example: The pupils found the lesson abstract, as they were asked to argue about a city that does not exist.

def: So complicated and difficult to understand that only specialists can follow it
example: Most of us needed a diagram, because the explanation of the theory was too abstruse to take in at once.

def: Easy to reach, enter, understand or make use of
example: The school website is accessible from any device, and the reading room is open to all students.

def: Widespread praise and approval given publicly for something
example: The young violinist received acclaim after her solo at the county concert, and everyone asked for an encore.

def: A mark of honour or praise awarded for a special achievement
example: Receiving a gold medal at the swimming gala was the greatest accolade of her school career so far.

def: To gather a growing amount of something over a period of time
example: Dust had accumulated thickly on the old piano, and a stack of unopened post lay on the shelf.

def: Showing that the speaker thinks another person is to blame
example: When he asked about the missing homework, Jordan's tone was so accusatory that her friend stopped talking.

def: To say that someone has done something wrong or unlawful
example: The head teacher refused to accuse anyone of cheating until the exam papers had been checked again.

def: To make someone used to something by giving them experience of it
example: It took several weeks to accustom the new starters to school life, and one girl still arrives far too early.

def: Harsh and bitter in tone, especially in speech or writing
example: His acerbic reply made the whole class laugh, though the teacher winced at its cruelty.

def: To make someone known to another, or to become known to them
example: You should acquaint yourself with the library rules before borrowing your first book this term.

def: Agreement given without really objecting or trying to change anything
example: His acquiescence went no further than a shrug, and he refused to help plan the event.

def: To get or gain something, or a new skill or quality
example: You can acquire a lot of confidence by joining the school choir and singing in front of others.

def: Full of bitterness, usually about a long-running disagreement
example: The meeting turned acrimonious after ten minutes, and two committee members walked out shouting.

def: A word formed from the first letters of a group of words, used as a short label
ant: full form; long form; written-out version
example: The instructions were packed with acronyms, so the coach explained each one before the foreign trip.

def: Completely determined not to change your mind or give way
example: She was adamant about wearing trainers to the ceremony, despite all the arguments from her parents.

def: To speak or write directly to a particular person or group
example: Please address your questions to the head teacher, as she deals with the bus route.

def: Enough in quantity, or good enough in quality, to be satisfactory
example: The shelter offers adequate room for forty people, but there is not enough parking nearby.

def: Someone who supports a belief, cause or leader
example: Every adherent of the cycling club must attend the safety talk before borrowing a bike.

def: Next to or immediately beside something
example: Our classroom is adjacent to the library, so we can borrow books between lessons.

def: To stop a meeting for a time and start it again later
example: The match was adjourned when the fog closed in, and the teams went home disappointed.

def: Deserving praise for something good or brave that has been done
example: It was admirable that Priya stayed behind to clear up after the storm, though she was exhausted.

def: Permission to enter a place or join a group
example: The museum charges no admission fee for pupils, but you must book a place online.

def: To speak to someone seriously because their behaviour was wrong or careless
example: The referee admonished the striker for a foul tackle, and a yellow card followed seconds later.

def: To take a child into your family as your own, or to start using a particular plan
example: His parents agreed to adopt the rescue puppy, and he chose a name for him on the first night.

def: To love and respect someone or something very much
example: My sister adores her violin teacher and practises faithfully for an hour every evening.

def: Excessive praise or flattery, often given to someone in power
example: Squads of photographers waited for the winner, offering adulation with every smile and handshake.

def: To move forward, or to make progress towards a goal
example: Reading daily will advance your writing, so the library runs a quiet club at lunchtime.

def: A person or group who opposes or competes against someone
example: Our adversaries from the neighbouring school made the final match exhausting, and neither team could rest.

def: Concerned with beauty and artistic taste rather than practical use
example: The building is admired for its aesthetic qualities, though the heating barely works in winter.

def: Showing that you care about someone and feel warmth and love for them
example: Her affectionate greeting with a gentle hug made everyone in the room feel welcome that afternoon.

def: A natural liking for something, or a close connection with it
example: She has an affinity for old maps, spending hours tracing coastlines in the library atlas.

def: A clear statement that something is true, which gives support to it
example: Her affirmation of the plan was recorded in the minutes, and nobody voted against it.

def: A condition of great pain or suffering
example: A bad tooth caused her such affliction that she missed the whole school trip.

def: Having plenty of money and a comfortable standard of living
example: The affluent family paid for three laptops so that each child had one at home.

def: Something said or done that openly insults someone's dignity
example: She considered his curt remark at the party an affront, and she left the room without a word.

def: A person who starts an attack, argument or act of hostility
example: The aggressor in the fight was suspended for a week, and the other boy received a caution.

def: So shocked by something terrible that you feel unable to respond
example: The whole class was aghast when a window shattered two centimetres from someone's head.

def: Someone who believes that the existence of God cannot be proved or disproved
example: When asked about religion at the fair, the scientist calmly said she was agnostic and left it there.

def: Pleasant in manner and easy to get on with, or happy to accept a suggestion
example: Our new neighbour was agreeable about the fence, and soon both families were sharing a barbecue.
